A client compares the adviser's fee with a 'free' online tip service. A fair response is to explain that:
Tip services are illegal and every user will face prosecution
Advice is personalised, fiduciary and accountable
The adviser guarantees returns, unlike the tip service
The adviser's fee is negotiable to zero if the client insists
An adviser's value lies in personalised, suitable advice with fiduciary duty and regulatory accountability. The adviser should avoid exaggerated claims or guarantees.
Documenting each client meeting in the CRM matters mainly because it:
Lets the sales team share client details on social media
Replaces the need for a written advisory agreement
Guarantees that the client will renew
Supports continuity, compliance and suitability records
Records of discussions, preferences and decisions support service continuity when staff change and demonstrate compliance with the adviser's suitability and record-keeping requirements.
A client insists on buying a stock tipped by a social media influencer. The best approach for sales staff is to:
Refer the request to the adviser for suitability review
Immediately agree and help the client buy as much as possible
Ridicule the client for following social media advice
Recommend a more speculative stock instead
Sales staff should not give their own recommendations. The adviser can assess suitability and explain risks, including unregistered persons' recommendations.
Active listening during client meetings involves:
Planning your next pitch while the client is speaking
Interrupting to correct the client quickly
Focusing only on figures and ignoring concerns
Paraphrasing and clarifying what the client says
Active listening means giving full attention, summarising the client's points and asking clarifying questions. It helps uncover real needs and builds trust.
Closing an advisory engagement ethically means:
Persuading the client to sign before reading the agreement
Offering gifts to encourage a quick signature
Hiding the fee structure until after the first invoice
Confirming the client understands terms, fees and risks before agreeing
Ethical closing ensures informed consent: the client knows the services, fees and risks. Pressure, inducements or hidden fees breach regulations and trust.

Professionalism, Ethics & Compliance.overview: This chapter covers the regulatory and ethical framework for investment advice: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 as amended, registration and qualification requirements, fiduciary duty, segregation of advisory and distribution activities, fee limits and modes, client agreement and risk profiling, disclosures, use of AI tools, record keeping, the role of the IA Administration and Supervisory Body, grievance redressal, and the limits on what non-core staff may do. Focus on prohibited practices and on the responsibilities of persons in sales and support roles.
questions: Under SEBI's segregation requirement, an individual investment adviser:
May earn commissions from products recommended to advisory clients
May act as both adviser and distributor if the client agrees orally
Must earn all its income from distribution commissions
Cannot provide distribution services to its advisory clients
SEBI requires advisory and distribution to be segregated at the client level, so advice is not influenced by commissions. Advisory clients cannot be offered distribution services.
An investment adviser's client agreement must cover:
Promise of a minimum annual return to the client
The client's waiver of the right to complain
The adviser's right to trade in the client's account at will
Terms of services, fees and the adviser's obligations
SEBI requires a client agreement with prescribed terms covering services, fees, conflicts, and obligations. Assured returns and waivers of client rights are not permitted.
Fees charged by an investment adviser to clients must be paid through:
Banking channels, such as cheques or online transfers
Cash handed over at the client's home
Gift cards and vouchers
Cryptocurrency transfers
Fees must be paid through traceable banking channels; cash is not permitted. SEBI's centralised fee collection mechanism further helps ensure payment only to registered advisers.
A sales staff member at an advisory firm is asked by a client to recommend a mutual fund scheme. The staff member should:
Recommend whichever scheme has the highest recent return
Recommend a scheme from the staff member's personal portfolio
Give advice as long as the client signs a waiver
Direct the request to a qualified adviser
Personal investment advice must come from qualified persons associated with investment advice. Non-core staff should route such requests to the adviser.
Which body has SEBI recognised as the Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB)?
The Association of Mutual Funds in India
The Reserve Bank of India
The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
BSE Limited
SEBI recognised BSE Limited, through a subsidiary, as IAASB to administer and supervise investment advisers. It handles enlistment, monitoring and complaint escalation.
An investment adviser using AI tools to generate advice must:
Avoid any disclosure, as AI use is a trade secret
Pass responsibility for any errors to the AI provider
Obtain the client's consent to waive suitability
Disclose AI use and remain responsible for the advice
SEBI's amended framework requires advisers to disclose AI use to clients and holds the adviser responsible for the advice, data security and compliance.
An investment adviser must carry out risk profiling of clients mainly to:
Decide how much commission to earn
Choose the client's tax regime
Replace KYC verification
Ensure that advice is suitable
Risk profiling assesses capacity and tolerance so that recommendations match the client. It is separate from KYC and from any commission considerations, which IAs cannot earn.
A sales executive tells a client that a recommended portfolio 'cannot lose money'. This statement is:
Misleading and prohibited
Acceptable if said only verbally
Required to build client confidence
Allowed for conservative portfolios
Assuring returns or no loss misrepresents risk and breaches SEBI's code of conduct. All investments carry risk, and communications must be fair and balanced.
